source: lib/mem.c:___INTR_GC publication after processor-0 GC phases
cases.scope: Finite one-runner, one-child, one-file progress witness. The positive initializer is a hash-bound copy of the unit-test runner: it enables public gc-report-set! in that child before the original file, reads public process-pid on that child's port, and forwards one completed GC report on the runner's own stderr with a fresh nonce, that pid, and that file. The stock runner's read-until-eof is a separate negative. VM-total last-gc-alloc includes observer allocation; mutatorKnown has no establishing action. Renewal requires a strict cursor advance through the existing progress shape. Child begin, a restored or regressed cursor, a wrong pid, source, or epoch, an incomplete collection, hidden interference, a failed exit, and a claim that another GC or TFIB root must occur are negative controls. File-exit admission stays exit 0 with the original stdout protocol and a cursor of at most one. This is not processor-membership refinement, not a TFIB-root or termination proof, and not native admission.
